result_summary:
ill working on it. From your screenshot, the problems are:
- **Links:** the footer links and phone numbers use the theme's blue on the navy background.
- **Form heading:** "We'll reply within 12 hours" is dark navy on navy, so it's nearly invisible.
- **Facebook icon:** it is dark on dark.

I've asked the designer to make the link text light with a white hover, make the form heading white, and make the icon visible. The designer is also checking the rest of the footer for other low-contrast text. Nothing is changed yet, so I'll confirm the result when it finishes. The edit will be in `Metadata_Model/page_models/model_surz_site_footer.json`.I edited `/Users/kandarpbaghar/.twasta/projects/08254d2c-ef7e-44a5-a5c3-a26004aedc6a/Surzion_Store/Metadata_Model/page_models/model_surz_site_footer.json`. I haven't rendered it, so the contrast is unchecked. Whether the per-block keys take effect is also unconfirmed, because the smart_pages skill documents no button text-colour key and no section-scoped palette override.

**What I changed**
- **Link buttons:** I changed `page.theme.palette.link` from `#2F6BE6` to `#C9D6F2` and `linkHover` from `#14307A` to `#FFFFFF`. This is the main fix, because the link variant takes its colour from the theme. It applies to the whole page, which is safe here because the footer's only section is dark.
- **Button groups:** I added `style: { "textColor": "#C9D6F2", "hover": { "textColor": "#FFFFFF" } }` to `fphones`, `fshop`, `facc` and `fpol`. This is a backup in case the palette change doesn't reach the buttons. `style.textColor` and `style.hover.textColor` are documented for blocks in general, but the skill never says whether `button_group` uses them.
- **Form heading:** I added `style: { "textColor": "#FFFFFF" }` to the `finq` form. If the form block ignores `style.textColor`, the heading will stay dark. In that case the fix has to come from the form renderer, or the heading has to become a separate `heading` block above the form.
- **Facebook icon:** I added `style: { "textColor": "#FFFFFF" }` to the `ffol` social_links block. Same caveat: the skill doesn't say whether `social_links` uses it.

**Left as is**
- **Form inputs:** The skill documents no style options for form field fills or borders, so I left them. If you want lighter inputs, that needs a change to the form block's code.
- **Other footer text:** The tagline (`#C9D6F2`), the column headings (`#FFFFFF`) and the bottom lines (`#9DB8F5`, about 6:1 on navy) already pass 4.5:1. No content, links or structure changed.

You can open the page in the workbench to preview it. If any of the three uncertain keys doesn't take effect, tell me which one.I've made the footer text lighter, but I haven't rendered it. Please reload the footer and check it. Three of the changes depend on settings the platform docs don't confirm, so they may not take effect.

**What changed**
- **Links:** I changed the page's link colour from blue to light blue (`#C9D6F2`), with white on hover. This should be the main fix for the links, phone numbers and policy links. It applies to the whole footer page, whose only section is the dark footer. I also set the same colours directly on the four link groups as a backup.
- **Form heading:** I set "We'll reply within 12 hours" to white.
- **Facebook icon:** I set the icon to white.

**What may not take effect:** the white form heading, the white Facebook icon and the direct link-group colours rely on a style setting the docs don't confirm those blocks use. If the heading is still dark, I'll turn it into a separate heading block above the form. If the icon is still dark, tell me and I'll look at it again.

**Not changed:** the form inputs still have a dark fill with faint borders, because the form block has no documented option for them. Your screenshot shows the labels are readable, so I left them. The rest of the footer text already has enough contrast.
